headline: Take-Two Interactive slumps 4.4% last night while oil crashes 5.3%, but the ASX held up reasonably well today — and Google just dropped a major new AI model.

portfolio.summary: The big mover overnight was Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), which dropped sharply — likely on broader market jitters rather than company-specific news. Google (GOOGL) also fell over 1% last night. On the ASX today, your holdings barely budged — CBA and VGE edged slightly higher, while VTS dipped a touch in line with the US market drag. FUEL.AX slipped marginally as oil prices fell hard overnight.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Dropped sharply last night — down over $10 a share. No major company news to explain it, so this looks like general market selling or sector rotation. GTA 6 hype is still building, but that hasn't been enough to prop up the price right now.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Fell $4.69 last night despite strong recent earnings. The drop seems to be broader tech profit-taking rather than anything Google-specific. In fact, Google announced a major new AI model today (Gemini Omni) which could be a positive catalyst.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Edged lower today on the ASX, reflecting crude oil's big fall overnight. OPEC also cut its global oil demand forecast for 2026, which is weighing on energy stocks.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Small gain at today's close — emerging markets getting a slight lift from the rising Aussie dollar and steady global sentiment.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Modest dip at today's ASX close, reflecting last night's mixed US session. Not a concern — just tracking the US market's minor moves.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
movers.note: Barely moved today — essentially flat at $164.73. CBA continues to hold near all-time highs with no fresh news to push it either way.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ finished slightly higher — a quiet, positive session. But the big story was crude oil, which crashed over 5% to $91.53 a barrel. That's a meaningful drop and it hit energy stocks hard. Gold meanwhile crept up, and the Aussie dollar strengthened slightly against the US dollar. Here in Australia, the ASX 200 closed down about 0.4% today — not a big sell-off, just a bit of softness.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Mild dip today — nothing alarming, just a quiet down day for the local market.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session was quietly positive — the broad US market edged higher.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Also finished slightly up last night, despite some big-name tech stocks pulling back.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Biggest market move of the day — oil dropped over 5% last night. OPEC cut its 2026 demand forecast and broader supply concerns eased, sending prices lower. Bad for FUEL.AX, but good news for inflation.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Nudged higher last night — investors still treating it as a safe haven amid global uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly — traders are betting the RBA won't need to raise rates as aggressively as feared.

politics.summary: Australian politics today was dominated by two big economic stories: Labor is pushing ahead with changes to capital gains tax (CGT — the tax you pay when you sell an asset like shares or property for a profit) and negative gearing (the tax break landlords get when their rental property runs at a loss), and they're linking these changes to popular income tax cuts. Meanwhile, there's a lively debate about whether the Reserve Bank should be raising interest rates.

stories.title: Labor ties popular tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: Labor is bundling income tax cuts with changes to CGT and negative gearing — meaning if you want the tax cuts, you may have to accept changes to the property and investment tax rules too. This is a big deal for property investors and anyone holding shares or investment assets. The CGT changes could affect how much tax you pay if you sell investments.

stories.title: Labor to ignore call for pause on CGT changes
stories.why_it_matters: Despite calls from industry groups and some experts to hit pause on the proposed CGT changes, Labor is pressing ahead. If you're thinking about selling investments or property, the timing of these changes is worth watching closely.

stories.title: 'Get on with it': Expert defies consensus and demands RBA hikes rates
stories.why_it_matters: One expert is bucking the trend and calling on the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) to lift interest rates — meaning higher mortgage repayments for borrowers. Most economists disagree, and markets are actually pricing in rate cuts later this year. Worth keeping an eye on the RBA's next move.

stories.title: RBA rate rise bets and government debt fears unwind, triggering demand for Australian bonds
stories.why_it_matters: Investors are now less worried about the RBA hiking rates and less spooked by government debt levels — and that's pushing more money into Australian government bonds. This is a sign the market is feeling calmer about Australia's economic outlook, which is generally good for Aussie assets.

ai.summary: The big AI headline today is Google dropping 'Gemini Omni' — a new flagship AI model. Meanwhile, the new Pope Leo XIV made global waves by issuing a sweeping call for international regulation of AI, specifically warning that autonomous weapons (military systems that can make kill decisions without a human in the loop) are already beyond effective human control.

stories.title: Introducing Gemini Omni — Google's new flagship AI model
stories.why_it_matters: Google just announced Gemini Omni — its most capable AI model yet. It's designed to handle text, images, audio, and video all at once (what the industry calls 'multimodal'). This is directly relevant to your GOOGL holding — it keeps Google competitive with OpenAI's GPT-4o and Anthropic's Claude. A strong AI product line helps justify Google's premium valuation.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV issues sweeping call for AI regulation and ethical oversight
stories.why_it_matters: The new Pope has used his first major official document (called an encyclical — basically a formal letter to the world's 1.4 billion Catholics) to call for urgent global regulation of AI. He's particularly alarmed by autonomous weapons — drones and military systems that can decide to fire without a human pressing a button. This adds significant moral and political weight to the global AI regulation debate, which could eventually shape rules that affect big tech companies like Google and Microsoft.

stories.title: Pope Leo warns autonomous weapons now impossible to govern
stories.why_it_matters: The Pope isn't just calling for light-touch rules — he's saying some AI-powered weapons systems are already out of human control. This is a striking statement from one of the world's most influential figures, and it's likely to accelerate political pressure on governments to regulate AI more aggressively. Keep an eye on how this shapes policy in the EU and US.

sport.summary: NRL Round 13 team news is the big local story, with injury chaos hitting the Warriors and Tigers. In AFL, the Brisbane Lions' big win has reignited debate about the competition's structure, and Neale Daniher — one of footy's most beloved figures — is getting tributes after stepping back from public life. And a surfing contest in New Zealand was stopped after an Aussie photographer was bitten by what's believed to be a shark or sea lion.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 teams: Warriors and Tigers hit with major injury blows
stories.why_it_matters: Big injury news heading into Round 13 — the Warriors have lost a key player ('that's my footy done'), and the Tigers are also doing it tough. State of Origin selection is also creating lineup uncertainty across several clubs. Worth checking your NRL draw before locking in any tips.

stories.title: Lions' slaughter exposes AFL's biggest farce — calls to fix the competition
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane's big win has sparked a fresh debate about whether the AFL finals system is fair and whether some competitions are too lopsided. Gerard Healy is calling for structural changes — it's the kind of debate that flares up every time a powerhouse team runs riot.

stories.title: Neale Daniher: Fighter, fundraiser, family — a legacy greater than football
stories.why_it_matters: A lovely tribute to Neale Daniher, the former Melbourne coach who has spent years fighting MND (Motor Neurone Disease) and raising tens of millions for research. One of football's most inspiring figures.

stories.title: World Surf League event in NZ halted after Australian photographer bitten by 'shark or sea lion'
stories.why_it_matters: A WSL surfing event in New Zealand was suspended after an Australian photographer was bitten in the water — suspected shark or sea lion. A sharp reminder of the risks for water sports competitors and spectators, even in seemingly safe locations.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Sharp drop — hold for now, GTA 6 still the long-term thesis
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 4.4% last night with no clear company-specific bad news. The GTA 6 release is still the big catalyst to watch. No reason to sell into this dip, but equally no reason to add more until we see a clearer price floor. Keep holding and watch for any GTA 6 release date or pre-order news.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Gemini Omni launch is a positive signal
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 1.2% last night, but the launch of Gemini Omni today is a real positive for the long-term story. Google is staying competitive in the AI race. The stock dip looks like general market noise, not a signal to sell. Hold confidently.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil down 5% — keep an eye on energy this week
watch_today.detail: Crude oil had its biggest single-day drop in months last night, falling to $91.53. OPEC also cut its 2026 demand forecast. FUEL.AX only fell 0.7% today, which shows some resilience, but if oil keeps sliding this week, expect more pressure on your energy ETF. Nothing to act on yet, but watch the oil price.

watch_today.title: Labor's CGT changes — relevant for your investments
watch_today.detail: Labor is pushing ahead with changes to how capital gains tax (the tax on profits when you sell assets like shares) is calculated, and they're bundling this with income tax cuts to make it politically sticky. If these changes pass, it could affect how much tax you pay when you eventually sell holdings like GOOGL, TTWO, or your ETFs. Worth talking to your accountant about the timing of any planned sales.

watch_today.title: Gold at $4,542 — your VDHG and VETS hold some indirect exposure
watch_today.detail: Gold hit $4,542 last night, continuing its strong run. While you don't hold gold directly, VDHG's diversified mix and global market ETFs benefit from the broader 'safe haven' sentiment that drives gold higher. Just good context to have.
